findings.title: Server header present but no version
findings.description: Server header present without version disclosure.

findings.title: Directory listing not detected
findings.description: /static/ does not appear to expose a directory listing.

findings.title: PostgreSQL port 5432 not exposed on host
findings.description: Port 5432 is not accessible from the host.
findings.evidence: TCP connection to localhost:5432 refused or timed out

findings.title: HSTS header missing
findings.description: The Strict-Transport-Security header is not present.
findings.evidence: Header 'Strict-Transport-Security' not found in response from http://localhost:8081
findings.risk: Without HSTS, browsers may connect over HTTP, enabling downgrade attacks.
findings.recommendation: Add 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains' to nginx configuration.

findings.title: CORS header absent
findings.description: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header present — cross-origin requests are not explicitly permitted.

findings.title: Cookie sets Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite
findings.description: The cookie includes the Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite attributes.

findings.title: No WAF detected in front of the application
findings.description: An obvious XSS/SQLi payload was not blocked; no web application firewall appears to be filtering requests.
findings.evidence: Attack payload returned HTTP 200 (expected 403/406 if a WAF were present)
findings.risk: Without a WAF, exploit attempts reach the application directly, removing a layer of defence-in-depth.
findings.recommendation: Deploy a WAF such as ModSecurity with the OWASP Core Rule Set in front of the app (see docs/WAF.md).

findings.title: No dangerous HTTP methods enabled
findings.description: The server does not advertise TRACE, TRACK, CONNECT, PUT, or DELETE.

findings.title: HTTP is not redirected to HTTPS
findings.description: Plain HTTP request returned HTTP 200 without redirecting to HTTPS.
findings.risk: Traffic served over plain HTTP can be intercepted or modified (MITM) and is exposed to SSL-stripping downgrade attacks.
findings.recommendation: Configure the web server to 301-redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS, and pair it with HSTS.

limitations: This is a local educational lab — not a production security audit.
This is not a penetration test.
Results require manual validation before any action.
Port checks only test localhost — not representative of network exposure.
